scripts.label: Tactic discovered attack missed
scripts.text: Another move offered a discovered attack. Moving a piece aside would uncover a threat from another.

scripts.label: Tactic double attack played
scripts.text: The idea is to make two attacks at once. Watch how the attacking pieces work together.

scripts.label: Tactic double attack allowed
scripts.text: This gives the other side a chance to make two attacks at once. Watch how those threats work together.

scripts.label: Tactic double attack missed
scripts.text: A stronger move offered a way to make two attacks at once. This move misses that chance.

scripts.label: Tactic deflection played
scripts.text: A deflection is the idea here: draw a defender away from its job, then use the opening it leaves.

scripts.label: Tactic deflection allowed
scripts.text: This gives the other side a chance to draw a defender away. That's a deflection: the defender leaves something important behind.

scripts.label: Tactic deflection missed
scripts.text: Another move could have drawn a defender away from its job. That was the chance to use a deflection.

scripts.label: Tactic undefended capture played
scripts.text: Look for the chance to take an undefended piece. Loose pieces are worth checking before settling on a move.

scripts.label: Tactic undefended capture missed
scripts.text: Another move offered a chance to take an undefended piece. This move lets it pass; keep an eye on loose pieces.

scripts.label: Tactic hanging piece allowed
scripts.text: This gives the other side a chance to take an undefended piece. Look for what could be left without protection.

scripts.label: Cause abandoned defender
scripts.text: This move takes away a piece's only effective defender. Now the other side can capture what was left behind.

scripts.label: Cause opponent threat recognition
scripts.text: The warning was in the opponent's previous move. This leaves that threat unanswered, and a piece can now be captured.

scripts.label: Positional development alternative
scripts.text: Another move would have brought a minor piece into play from its starting square.

scripts.label: Positional rook open alternative
scripts.text: Another move would have left a rook on a file with no pawns. That's an open file.

scripts.label: Positional rook semi open alternative
scripts.text: Another move would have left a rook on a semi-open file, with enemy pawns there but none of its own.

scripts.label: Positional passed alternative
scripts.text: Another move would have left a passed pawn, with no enemy pawn ahead on its file or the neighboring files.

scripts.label: Positional passer advance actual
scripts.text: The pawn was already passed; this move advances it. Take a moment to follow its progress.

scripts.label: Positional passer advance alternative
scripts.text: Another move would have pushed the passed pawn forward. See where it could have gone.

scripts.label: Positional isolated alternative
scripts.text: Another move would have left an isolated pawn. It would have no friendly pawn on either neighboring file.

scripts.label: Positional support alternative
scripts.text: Another move would have given a piece a defender. It would no longer be left on its own.
